name: Stefan Maron PTE non-schema deletion rules
description: Downgrades deletion and obsolete lifecycle rules for non-schema objects to Warning. Schema-affecting deletions (AS0001, AS0002, AS0009, AS0010, AS0041, AS0043) are intentionally excluded and remain Errors. PTEs can legitimately remove UI elements and code objects without risking data loss or deployment failures.

rules.justification: Procedures can be removed in PTEs without schema risk.
Pages and page extensions can be removed in PTEs without schema risk.
Actions can be removed in PTEs without schema risk.
Controls can be removed in PTEs without schema risk.
Views can be removed in PTEs without schema risk.
Interface implementations can be removed in PTEs without schema risk.
Interfaces can be removed in PTEs without schema risk.
ObsoleteTag requirement is a lifecycle ceremony, not a data protection rule.
ObsoleteTag ordering is a lifecycle ceremony, not a data protection rule.
ObsoleteReason requirement is a lifecycle ceremony, not a data protection rule.
ObsoleteTag consistency on objects is a lifecycle ceremony, not a data protection rule.
ObsoleteTag consistency on fields/keys is a lifecycle ceremony, not a data protection rule.
Code objects with IDs (codeunits, reports, queries, enums) can be removed in PTEs without schema risk.
Code objects without IDs that can be referenced can be removed in PTEs without schema risk.
ObsoleteState transition ordering is a lifecycle ceremony. PTEs can skip Pending and go directly to Removed.
